title: The Case of the Missing Biscuit Label
markdown:
Coach Fern, bless her organized heart, had a vision. She pictured perfectly clean cupboards and neatly labelled shelves. She wanted the scout hut to be so tidy you could hear a pin drop. Of course, in this particular scout hut, that pin had probably been borrowed by a goat.

The focus of Coach Fern’s intense organizing was the "Miscellaneous Cupboard." It was a messy space filled with forgotten camping gear, leftover craft supplies, and the occasional runaway sock. This cupboard showed how well the scouts were at leaving things in odd spots.

"Right, troop!" Coach Fern announced. Her voice was as chirpy as a robin ready for breakfast. She stood with her hands on her hips, dressed in sensible tweed. "Today, we'll bring order to this mess! Today, we label!"

Then came Arlo the goat. His main job was usually to make things messy, not tidy. He was trying to balance a scout handbook on his horns. Its pages fluttered like tiny, confused birds. His curious eyes scanned the room, already spotting things he might like to nibble. Beside him, Cleo the cat watched with her usual bored expression. Her tail gave a slow, thoughtful swish, as if to say, "This might be slightly interesting."

Coach Fern showed off her prize: a label maker, shiny and new. She wasn't just labelling shelves; she was writing little stories for each item. The crumpled tin foil became: "Glimmering Wrapper, holder of campfire stories and accidental bird feeders. Its shiny surface once made a squirrel blink twice." The old skipping rope was labelled: "Springy String, once used in a legendary double-dutch game that ended in a spectacular tie and three very dizzy scouts."

The scouts, who were at first surprised by this new way of tidying, quickly became hooked. They’d spend ages reading the labels, laughing at the clever jokes and surprisingly accurate descriptions.

"This rusty compass," young Pipkin read aloud, frowning in concentration, "once pointed North, then South, then towards Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning petunias. Its sense of direction is… creative, we'll say." A wave of giggles spread through the group.

Arlo, however, was more interested in the labels themselves. He found their papery texture quite tasty. He proved this by trying to munch on: "Sticky Tape, guardian of torn maps and surprise bandages. It holds on tightly, just like a badger protecting its home."

Cleo nudged him with her head, letting out a sigh that sounded like a soft purr of disapproval. "Honestly, Arlo. So uncouth. You’d think you’d have better taste, for a creature who claims to appreciate the elegant crunch of a dandelion stem."

The real problem started with the Emergency Biscuit Tin. This wasn't just any tin; it was Coach Fern's special collection, saved for times of great scout-related sadness. This happened when the map for finding their way dissolved in the rain, or when someone accidentally created a new kind of super-sticky mud that clung to the ceiling. The label on this tin was a work of art. It read: "The Last Hope Tin: Holds food for tired souls and a sprinkle of never-give-up hope. Do Not Open, unless you’ve lost all hope (and maybe your snacks). May contain traces of pure, delightful yumminess." Coach Fern often said it was the most important thing in the whole hut, right after the first-aid kit and her secret stash of spare shoelaces.

One windy Tuesday, as the scouts were trying to learn new knots, a shared gasp went through the hut. The Emergency Biscuit Tin sat on its shelf, but its label… its label was gone. A worried feeling spread through everyone. The biscuit tin looked bare and unprotected, like a king without his crown. A quiet fell, only broken by the wind sighing through a gap in the window.

"My label!" Coach Fern cried out. Her organized world felt like it was crumbling like a stale biscuit. Her usual cheerful voice sounded wobbly. "The heart of the cupboard! Who could have taken it? Did it wander off looking for adventure? Perhaps it ran away with the label from the spare batteries?"

Arlo, who had been nervously chewing his tail (a habit he had when he was stressed), suddenly looked up. He nudged Cleo with his wet nose. "Something's missing," he bleated, his ears twitching as if trying to catch a signal.

Cleo stretched. "Indeed. And knowing you, Arlo, I suspect you've either eaten or hidden the missing item in that large hole you call a home. Though, this time, it feels… different. There's a distinct smell of worry in the air, not just your usual scent of damp hay and silly ideas."

A search party quickly formed. The scouts, their earlier fun replaced with a sense of duty, spread out. Arlo, with his good nose, sniffed the air like a detective on a case. "Biscuit," he declared. Then, after a moment of deep thought, "Paper-y biscuit. And… something shy. Like a little mouse at a big party."

Cleo, from her higher perch, scanned the ceiling beams. Her green eyes missed nothing. "Nothing up here. Though there is a rather dusty spider who seems to be having a deep conversation with a cobweb about how short life is. He looks quite thoughtful, actually."

They searched the whole hut. The "Sparkling Lantern, for lighting up dark evenings and finding lost beetles. Its light has been known to scare away pretend monsters and at least one real moth," offered no hints. The "Wobbly Tent Pegs, experts at leaning in funny ways, giving your tent an artistic look," were no help at all.

As they searched carefully, Arlo stopped by the new-scouts corner. It was a small, slightly sad area where new people usually met the troop. He nudged a shy-looking new scout named Lily. Lily clutched a well-loved book to her chest. She had only joined last week and still seemed to be finding her way, like a baby deer on a slippery patch of grass.

"What is it, Arlo?" Coach Fern asked, her voice showing her worry. She was starting to eye the spare biscuit tin, wondering if it had somehow managed to escape.

Arlo pointed his nose at Lily’s book. Tucked between its pages, as if being kept safe, was the missing label. Lily’s cheeks turned as pink as a ripe raspberry. She held her book a little tighter.

"I… I borrowed it," she whispered, her voice so quiet it was like dry leaves rustling. "The stories on the labels… they're so interesting. I wanted to read about the biscuits. And… and I felt a bit lost, and the label made the tin look important. I thought if something so important had a story, maybe I would have a story here too."

A hush fell over the scouts. The wind seemed to pause. Coach Fern’s stern face softened. She knelt beside Lily, her tweed skirt rustling. "Oh, my dear," she said gently, her voice as warm as a fresh cookie. "You didn't need to borrow the label to find your story here. You're part of the story now. All of us are. Every single one of us brings our own special chapter to the Hemlock Hollow Scouts."

She carefully picked up the label, smooth and cool in her hand. Arlo, feeling a little bad for suspecting Lily, nudged her hand with his head, a surprisingly gentle touch for a goat. Cleo, for once, stopped being distant and let out a soft, rumbling purr of approval, a sound of pure happiness.

The label was put back, and the Emergency Biscuit Tin was returned to its rightful, hopeful place. The scouts, their scare over, went back to their knots. A new understanding had dawned on them. The labels weren't just labels; they were small windows into the lives of their scout hut, and into the lives of each other. They were reminders that even ordinary things had a history, a purpose, and sometimes, a touch of fun. And for a shy new scout, a story about a tin of biscuits could be the most welcoming thing in the world, a sign that she belonged.

As for Arlo, he decided paper was best left to the labels, and that his own stories were best told with happy bleats and the occasional friendly head-butt. The Miscellaneous Cupboard, now full of tales about tin foil and compasses, stood as proof that even in the messiest places, stories – and biscuits – could always be found. And Coach Fern, looking at her troop, knew that true order wasn't just about tidy shelves, but about the happiness and stories of every single scout, especially the new ones. She also made a note to label her own emergency biscuit tin, just in case it decided to have a deep chat with the spare shoelaces.
characters: Arlo the goat, Cleo the cat, Coach Fern
